newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania airline selloff takes next step.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania airline selloff takes next step.

text.p: The privatisation of Lithuania's national airlines took a further step on Monday as the transport ministry approved a plan to merge the two companies.
The decision means larger Lithuanian Airlines will merge with smaller Aviation Company Lietuva and they will be sold off as one company.
An international tender is soon to be announced for financial companies to draw up the detailed privatisation programme for the airline, officials said.
"The transport ministry decided today to merge Lithuanian Airlines (LAL) and Aviation Company Lietuva into one," Transport Minister Algis Zhvaliauskas told Reuters.
"We have asked the civil aviation department of the ministry to draw up the necessary documents for the merger in the next 10 days," Zhvaliauskas added.
Zhvaliauskas also said that Lietuva will operate as a daughter company of LAL after the merger.
The government plans to keep at least 34 percent of the company and wants Lithuanian-registered businesses to own at least 51 percent, to keep it as a national carrier.
Zhvaliauskas said the merger would speed up the privatisation process of the two companies.
"During the privatisation, both companies will be sold as one," Zhvaliauskas said.
Lithuanian Airlines has share capital of 76.5 million litas while Lietuva has share capital of 2.8 million litas.
Lithuanian Airlines has three Boeing 737-200s, two SAAB 340Bs, A Jetstar and five TU-134s. It is currently in talks to sell its 11 JAK 42s to Pakistani airline, Bhoia Airline.
